The full test suite passes (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 3/3 tests green). The change is complete and well-structured.

## Summary

I implemented optional owner email support: **present ⇒ must be syntactically valid; stored and returned lower-cased; 400 when present but invalid.**

The logic mirrors the existing telephone design — a dedicated normalizer component invoked by the owner field validator — so no class became a catch-all and nothing was copied.

**Files changed:**

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added the optional `email` property to the `OwnerFields` schema, so the generated `OwnerFieldsDto`/`OwnerDto` gain the field (and MapStruct maps it automatically on both directions — no mapper edits needed).

2. **`model/Owner.java`** — added the `email` field with `@Column(name="email")`, getter/setter, and `toString` entry.

3. **`rest/controller/EmailNormalizer.java`** (new) — a small single-responsibility `@Component` mirroring `TelephoneNormalizer`: `isValid(...)` checks syntactic validity and `normalize(...)` lower-cases (using `Locale.ROOT`).

4. **`rest/controller/OwnerFieldsValidator.java`** — injects `EmailNormalizer`; when email is present it either writes back the lower-cased value or records a field error (which surfaces as a 400 via the existing binding-error handling). Absent email is left untouched.

5. **`rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — `updateOwner` now carries email through, keeping the update path consistent with create.

6. **DB schemas** (`hsqldb`, `h2`, `mysql`, `postgres`) — added a nullable `email` column. The hsqldb/mysql seed `data.sql` inserts used positional `VALUES(...)`, which any new column breaks, so I gave the `owners` inserts explicit column lists (h2/postgres already used them).

Validation and normalization live in one place, reusing the existing `@Valid`/`@InitBinder` pipeline rather than duplicating error handling.
